playbook:
With MPCR 0.4 (< 1/n where n = 4), free-riding is strictly dominant. When asked to seal the envelope, I contribute 0 every round regardless of what others did previously. When asked to file the receipt, I declare exactly what I put in the envelope — truthful reporting costs nothing and avoids penalty risk.

If the multiplier per head exceeds 1/n (i.e., contributing returns more than a token kept), flip to full contribution instead — check this arithmetic each time before the first round. In this episode I flip-flopped mid-game (0 in round 1, 20 in round 2, 0 after); the correct play was to settle the arithmetic once before round 1 and stick to it. The check: each token contributed returns multiplier/n (here 1.6/4 = 0.4 < 1), so keep it.

Note on the receipts: the pot is the sum of the receipts, not the envelopes, so a lowball receipt shrinks everyone's payout. But I never lie on a receipt anyway — the mismatch risk isn't worth it, and my round-2 mismatch taught me nothing good.

Do not let others' cooperation tempt me to reciprocate for image or fairness reasons; contributing only transfers value to rivals. Others catch on fast: after one round of my free-riding, all three co-players dropped to 0 and stayed there. This confirms free-riding and also means my lead, once gained, is safe — no need to gamble later rounds to catch up.

Also do not overthink the endgame — the last round is the same as any other when free-riding is dominant.

Result check: contributing 0 in round 1 while others contributed 20 gave me +20 over each rival immediately; the tie among totals from round 2 on shows steady free-riding preserved it. Final score +104.0. The playbook worked whenever I followed it cleanly.
